score_method: Minimum mandatory visual-area score, not an average; every mandatory static visual check must pass strictly above 9.0.
pending_separate_evidence: Full GitHub byte/blob readback and independent archive gate
preservation: All previous source identities, original accepted images, rejected iterations and exact prompts remain preserved.

areas.finding: The ordinary unarmored Atlas brown bear remains broad-shouldered with rounded ears, dark nose, pale brown muzzle and heavy visible-clawed paws. No companion saddle, armor, harness, chains or bags are introduced.
Four true cardinal directions and distinct front/rear obliques show the full body with ears, tail and paws inside the frame.

Four substantial legs and paws resolve through the profiles and front oblique. Natural rear oblique occlusion does not add or remove a limb. Paws meet the studio ground and visible claws belong to toes.
Round ears, broad muzzle, dark nose, expressive eyes and compact open mouth stay coherent across front and opposing profiles.
One small tail is attached high at the rump, visible in rear, profiles and rear oblique, without extra appendages.
Broad shoulders, shaggy neck, warm-brown mass and strong forelegs remain consistent. Cream-brown cheek groups and forehead markings retain their main placement.
Polished rounded sculpted fur, complete anatomy, clean illumination and readable labels provide a useful static animal reference.

source_interpretation_limit: The original Atlas supplies a small single-pose source appearance. Hidden reverse anatomy, fur grouping and fine texture placement are authored concept interpretation. Static sheets do not establish a native mesh, rig, animation or gameplay implementation.
minor_polish_limit: Fine fur-tuft placement and claw visibility vary with perspective; the sheet does not establish native topology, exact texture UVs or motion.
